title: KVL：绕一圈，电压加起来是 0
summary: 一个电源、三个电阻和一颗 LED 组成三个回路：沿任意回路走一圈，电压的代数和都是 0。
concepts: KVL 基尔霍夫电压定律
description: 用万用表测量每个元件两端的电压，验证基尔霍夫电压定律（KVL）：沿任意闭合回路绕一圈，各段电压的代数和为 0。电路：+9 V → R1（470 Ω）→ 结点 M；M 到 GND 有两条路：红色 LED，以及 R2（1 kΩ）→ 结点 X → R3（2.2 kΩ）。

cards.title: 找出三个圈
text: 先照目标电路图搭好：+9 V → **R1** → 结点 **M**；从 M 到 GND 有两条路——一颗 **LED**，以及 **R2 → X → R3**。
不急着量。用手指在图上找：从一个点出发、沿导线和元件走一圈回到原点，这样的**圈**有几个？

cards.title: KVL：上山的高度 = 下山的高度
text: - 把电压想成**高度**。沿着一个圈走，经过电源是“上山”，经过电阻、LED 是“下山”。回到原点时，高度一定和出发时一样。
- 所以：**沿任何闭合回路，电压的代数和为 0**。这就是基尔霍夫电压定律（KVL）。
- 这里有三个圈：① 电源 → R1 → LED；② LED 和 R2、R3 组成的圈（里面**没有电源**）；③ 电源 → R1 → R2 → R3。
![](fig:loops)
- 动手之前，先把三个圈的 KVL 方程写下来。想一想：LED 两端会正好是 1.8 V 吗？

cards.title: 量五段电压
text: - 万用表红表笔点一个元件的一端，**Shift + 单击**把黑表笔放在另一端，读数 = V(红) − V(黑)。
- 依次量电源、R1、LED、R2、R3。电路检查通过后，把读数填进测量题，再代入你的三个方程。

cards.title: 带走
text: - KVL 对 LED 这种**非线性**元件同样成立：它只管电压，不管元件的伏安特性。
- 回路 ② 说明：**并联的两条支路，两端电压一定相等**——这一点马上在并联里用到。
- 方程对不上时，先查两件事：表笔方向（读数的正负）、是不是量到了同一个元件的两端。

caption.text: 圈 ①：电源 → R1 → LED；圈 ②：LED → R2 → R3（没有电源）；圈 ③ 是外面的大圈：电源 → R1 → R2 → R3。

i18n.en: Loop ①: source → R1 → LED; loop ②: LED → R2 → R3 (no source); loop ③ is the outer one: source → R1 → R2 → R3.

en.title: KVL: around a loop, the voltages add up to 0
en.summary: One source, three resistors and an LED make three loops: around any loop the voltages add up to zero.
en.description: Measure the voltage across every part with the multimeter and verify Kirchhoff's voltage law (KVL): around any closed loop the voltages add up to zero. Circuit: +9 V → R1 (470 Ω) → node M; from M to GND there are two paths: a red LED, and R2 (1 kΩ) → node X → R3 (2.2 kΩ).
en.compare:
**Compare** (simulator readings):
- supply: 9.00 V
- R1: ≈ 7.03 V (current ≈ 14.95 mA)
- LED: ≈ 1.97 V (not 1.8 V: the LED model is 1.8 V plus 12Ω, and 14.3 mA × 12Ω ≈ 0.17 V)
- R2: ≈ 0.62 V, R3: ≈ 1.36 V (only 0.62 mA flows in this branch)

The three loops: ① 9.00 = 7.03 + 1.97; ② 1.97 = 0.62 + 1.36, i.e. once around, 1.97 − 0.62 − 1.36 = 0; ③ 9.00 = 7.03 + 0.62 + 1.36. If an equation does not balance, check the probe direction (the sign of the reading) and that you measured across the two ends of the same part.

measurements.ask: Voltage across R1, V_R1 (red lead on R1's supply end, black lead on M)
Voltage across the LED, V_LED (red lead on the long leg)
measurements.explain: Not 1.8 V: the LED model is 1.8 V plus 12 Ω, and about 14.3 mA × 12 Ω ≈ 0.17 V.

measurements.ask: Voltage across R2, V_R2 (red lead on the M side)
Voltage across R3, V_R3 (red lead on the X side)
Loop ② (no source): with your own three readings, V_LED − V_R2 − V_R3 =
measurements.explain: Round a loop the voltages add up to 0 — KVL holds for a non-linear part like the LED too. The few millivolts left over come from the digits of the readings.

hints: M is a node: one end of R1, the LED's long lead and one end of R2 must share a column (one metal strip).
The LED's short lead (cathode) and the far end of R3 both go to GND (the blue rail).
To measure R2: click the red probe onto R2's lead at M, then Shift + click the black probe onto R2's lead at X.
tests: LED on; loop 1: supply voltage = voltage across R1 + voltage across the LED
Loop 2 (no source): the LED's voltage = R2's voltage + R3's voltage

cards.title: Find the three loops
text: Build it from the target schematic: +9 V → **R1** → node **M**; from M to GND there are two paths — an **LED**, and **R2 → X → R3**.
No measuring yet. With your finger on the drawing: starting at a point and following wires and parts back to the same point, how many such **loops** are there?

cards.title: KVL: up the hill = down the hill
text: - Think of voltage as **height**. Walking around a loop, a source takes you "uphill" and resistors and LEDs take you "downhill". Back at the start, you are at the same height you left.
- So: **around any closed loop the voltages add up to zero**. That is Kirchhoff's voltage law (KVL).
- There are three loops here: ① source → R1 → LED; ② the LED with R2 and R3 (**no source** in it); ③ source → R1 → R2 → R3.
![](fig:loops)
- Before you measure, write the KVL equation of each loop. And think: will the LED show exactly 1.8 V?

cards.title: Measure five voltages
text: - Red probe on one end of a part, **Shift + click** to put the black probe on the other end; reading = V(red) − V(black).
- Measure the source, R1, the LED, R2 and R3. Once the circuit check passes, fill in the questions and plug the readings into your three equations.

cards.title: Take away
text: - KVL holds for a **nonlinear** part like an LED too: it is only about voltages, not about the part's voltage–current curve.
- Loop ② says **two branches in parallel always have the same voltage across them** — you will use that right away in parallel circuits.
- If an equation doesn't add up, check two things first: the probe direction (the sign of the reading) and that you measured across the same part.

回路 2（无电源）：LED 上的电压 = R2 上的电压 + R3 上的电压
